proposals.relationship: As Megan Hamilton reads the1999 response, Palmer contests Granatstein’s picture of a declining historical profession while also questioning the defensive self-satisfaction of its critics.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicit named mediation: Hamilton2021,28/notes44–45 identifies Palmer’s argument that historians are doing well and that defensive reaction to Granatstein has displaced critical reflection. The response is also directed at McKillop; Palmer is not flattened into McKillop’s camp. Original Palmer1999CHR80:4,676–686 and Granatstein’s1998book remain unread. Hamilton’s printed journal essay is a student scholarly publication, not treated as a direct reading of either original or as proof of every Palmer argument.
primary_locators: Megan Hamilton,The Intellectual Career of J.L.Granatstein,Waterloo Historical Review10(Autumn2021),28/notes44–45; her note locators3 and6–7 for Palmer are retained as her numbering, not silently converted into original journal pages.

proposals.relationship: Buckner contrasts Granatstein’s sweeping fragmentation charge with Owram’s more qualified pursuit of national synthesis that retains the value of recent social history.
proposals.evidence_note: Own fresh reading of Buckner2000,9: he explicitly groups their fragmentation diagnoses but distinguishes Owram’s willingness to take the last30years of scholarship seriously and his acceptance of social history. Buckner himself contests both the hierarchy of national versus subdisciplinary history and the premise that regional history fragments Canada. An attributed comparison, not an Owram attack on Granatstein or an intellectual transmission. Granatstein1998 and Owram1997 original bodies unread.
primary_locators: P.A.Buckner,Limited Identities and Other Nonsense: Regionalism and Nationalism in Canadian History,Acadiensis30:1(Autumn2000),9/notes17–19, continuing qualification10/n20.
